annotations.annotation_text: HCE manifestation "Earwicker" on page 108 within "The Letter from the Midden": here the universal father-figure Humphrey Chimpden Earwicker appears in the context of Biddy Doran the Hen scratching up the mysterious letter from the dump, the Book of Kells as model for textual exegesis. During this Age of Gods phase, HCE embodies the patriarch whose guilt, grandeur, and fall drive the cyclical dream forward.
sources: Glasheen, Adaline. Third Census of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/thirdcensusoffin0000glas
McHugh, Roland. The Sigla of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/siglaoffinnegans0000mchu
James Joyce Digital Archive: Finnegans Wake Notons. https://jjda.ie

annotations.annotation_text: Celtic/mythological figure "Fionn" on page 108 ("The Letter from the Midden"): invoking the ancient Fianna cycle and early Irish Christianity within Biddy Doran the Hen scratching up the mysterious letter from the dump, the Book of Kells as model for textual exegesis. During the Age of Gods phase, this mythic presence grounds the universal dream in Ireland's heroic past, linking Finn MacCool's giant body to the Dublin landscape.
sources: MacKillop, James. Dictionary of Celtic Mythology. https://www.oxfordreference.com
Lady Gregory. Gods and Fighting Men. https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/14465
O'Hehir, Brendan. A Gaelic Lexicon for Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/gaeliclexiconfor0000oheh
